flawed_step: The claimed threshold k = ceil(n/2) is insufficient: two tours can differ in more than k edges while every tour within k changes is no shorter.
counterexample: Let n=6 and k=3. On K6, set w12=w45=w13=w36=w46=0; w23=w34=w56=w16=1; w25=2; and w14=w15=w24=w26=w35=5. Consider C=(1,2,3,4,5,6,1), of cost 4. Any tour containing a weight-5 edge costs at least 5. Among tours using only the other ten edges and sharing at least three edges with C (equivalently, obtainable by a 3-change), the alternatives are (1,2,5,4,3,6,1), (1,2,5,6,4,3,1), and (1,3,2,5,4,6,1); each costs 4. Thus C is a 3-Opt local optimum. But D=(1,2,5,4,6,3,1) costs 2. It shares only edges 12 and 45 with C, so reaching it requires replacing four edges. Hence C is not globally optimal despite k=ceil(6/2)=3.
assessment_summary: A concrete six-city symmetric TSP instance has a 3-Opt local optimum of cost 4 and a global improvement of cost 2 requiring four edge replacements.
